bms_4168_0800d2ec.name: bms_protect_latch_evaluate
bms_4168_0800d2ec.summary: Evaluate eight dwell-timed threshold latches and update protection status word 0x20000254
bms_4168_0800d2ec.description: Runs the protection latch engine once per call over eight channels. Each channel has a trigger timer and a release timer (accumulators at 0x20000F20 to 0x20000F7C): while the channel's measurement is on its arming side of the threshold pair the trigger timer adds param_4, and when it reaches the channel limit the channel's status bit is set and the timer is clamped (bits 0x10, 0x02, 0x40, 0x200, 0x400, 0x4000, 0x20000 and 0x80000 for channels 1 to 8). A set latch clears through its release timer while the measurement is on the release side, and the clear masks also drop bits 0x04 and 0x08 that channels 1 and 2 share. Param_3 bit 0 sets status 0x08 and bit 1 sets status 0x1000 directly. At the end the status word is mirrored into the BMS state block: bits 1 to 8 into bit 3 of the 16-bit word at +0x124, bits 10 to 16 into bit 4 of +0x124, bits 19 to 22 into bit 4 of +0x126, bit 17 into bit 11 of +0x194, and bits 0, 9 and 18 into bits 4, 7 and 8 of +0x198.

params.name: param_1
params.description: measurement record: 16-bit values at +2 and +4 (+4 is the channel 1 input, +2 selects channel 5 thresholds)

params.name: param_2
params.description: measurement record: 32-bit value at +0, 16-bit values at +4, +8 and +0xE

params.name: param_3
params.description: flag word: bit 0 sets status 0x08, bit 1 sets status 0x1000

params.name: param_4
params.description: elapsed ticks added to the dwell timers while a channel is armed

bms_4168_0800d2ec.notes: Which measurement is compared against which limit and the threshold units are not identified; the arming side comes from the compares. Channel 5 picks its threshold from DAT_20000024 (values 6 to 8) and the sticky flag DAT_20000250. The accumulators 0x20000F20 to 0x20000F7C are not in this packet's RAM reference list and were taken from the decompile.

bms_4168_0800df2c.name: bms_txq_enqueue
bms_4168_0800df2c.summary: Queue a 9-byte message descriptor and payload into the first free of five pool slots
bms_4168_0800df2c.description: Claims the first pool slot at 0x20002B8C (20-byte stride, five slots) whose flag byte is nonzero, sets the flag to 0, and writes the four header bytes of the descriptor, the length byte (+8) and the payload (copied from the pointer at +4) into the slot's 12-byte record at the pointer stored in slot+4 (records at 0x20002B14, payload buffers at 0x20002614 + 0x80 * slot). The tag param_2 goes to slot+0xC and the slot is appended to the singly linked list headed by DAT_20002608, with the link at slot+0x10, while DAT_2000260C counts the entries. If an entry already in the list has the same header bytes 0 and 3, the new slot is released again (flag 1) and the call returns 0 as a duplicate. Part of the message pool group with bms_txq_init, bms_comm_service_step and bms_reply_buffer_get.

params.name: param_1
params.description: descriptor: bytes 0 to 3 header, pointer to the payload at +4, length byte at +8

params.name: param_2
params.description: tag stored at the slot's +0xC; callers pass a code address (LAB_080039d4_1 in bms_4168_0800e060)

returns.description: 1 when the message was appended; 0 for a duplicate, a full queue (count 5) or no free slot

bms_4168_0800df2c.notes: The length byte is not checked against the 128-byte payload buffer, so a length above 128 overruns into the next buffer. The tag is only stored here; the code that uses it is outside this packet.

bms_4168_0800dfec.name: bms_txq_init
bms_4168_0800dfec.summary: Reset the five-slot message pool, the queue head and counters, then stamp the periodic timer
bms_4168_0800dfec.description: Initialises the message request pool used by bms_txq_enqueue. For each of the five 20-byte slots at 0x20002B8C it sets the flag to 1 (free), points the slot's first record at 0x20002B14 + 12 * i and its second record at 0x20002B50 + 12 * i, sets the buffer pointers of those records to 128-byte buffers at 0x20002614 + 0x80 * i and 0x20002894 + 0x80 * i, and clears the tag and link words. It then clears the queue head DAT_20002608, the queue count DAT_2000260C, the service state bytes DAT_2000260D to DAT_20002611 and the busy flags DAT_20002612 and DAT_20002613, and stores the current time base from bms_tick_get in DAT_200025FC as the start of the periodic send timer. Part of the message pool group.

bms_4168_0800e060.name: bms_comm_service_step
bms_4168_0800e060.summary: Service the message pool: periodic 14-byte send, two busy timeouts, then dispatch the state handler
bms_4168_0800e060.description: Called once per service tick. It takes the elapsed ticks since DAT_200025FC from bms_tick_get (an extra tick is subtracted when the time base has wrapped) and, once more than 999 ticks have passed, enqueues a 14-byte message through bms_txq_enqueue with the header 0xB5 0x07 0x06 0x00 and the payload at 0x20002BF0; DAT_200025FC is restamped only if the enqueue succeeded. The busy flag DAT_20002612 is cleared, together with DAT_20002613, when more than 2999 ticks have passed since DAT_20002600; otherwise DAT_20002613 is cleared after 2999 ticks since DAT_20002604. It then calls the handler whose address is in the RAM table at 0x20000614 + 4 * DAT_2000260D, and returns 1 only when that state index is 0 and DAT_20002613 is clear, so 1 means idle. Part of the message pool group.

returns.description: 1 when the state index is 0 and DAT_20002613 is clear, else 0

bms_4168_0800e060.notes: The 1000 and 3000 constants are taken as 1 ms ticks, which is an assumption. The handler table at 0x20000614 is in RAM and is filled elsewhere. The subtract-one on wrap is kept as the compiler produced it and may be an off-by-one.

bms_4148_0800e228.name: bms_balance_timer_step
bms_4148_0800e228.summary: Advance the 30000-tick re-evaluation timer and update state bits 1 and 2 of DAT_20000504
bms_4148_0800e228.description: Advances a 30000-tick re-evaluation timer (DAT_20000510) for the state byte DAT_20000504. While bit 0 (enable) is clear it clears the timer and bit 1. While enabled it accumulates param_1, and when the timer reaches 30000 it restarts the timer and re-evaluates from the 16-bit values in the BMS state block at +0x104 (a percentage in which 100 means full), +0x11E and +0x19C. With bit 1 set it keeps the state while +0x104 is at or below +0x11E and otherwise clears bits 1 and 2; with bit 1 clear it clears bit 1 when the value is exactly 100, sets bit 2 when the value is at or below +0x19C (and bit 1 as well when it is at least 2 below), and clears bits 1 and 2 when it is above +0x19C. Present in the BMS_4130, BMS_4139 and BMS_4148 builds only.

params.name: param_1
params.description: elapsed ticks since the last call

bms_4148_0800e228.notes: The meaning of +0x104, +0x11E, +0x19C and of bits 1 and 2 is inferred from the timing and the comparisons; the function itself does not confirm it. The packet lists the state block accessor as bms_ram_20000bdc_addr, which is FUN_0800bb00 in this build.

bms_4168_0800e2a8.name: bms_reply_buffer_get
bms_4168_0800e2a8.summary: Return the 24-byte reply buffer at 0x20002BFE, clearing it while the busy flag is clear
bms_4168_0800e2a8.description: When the busy flag DAT_20002612 (used by bms_comm_service_step) is zero it clears the 24-byte buffer at 0x20002BFE through bms_4168_08001246, a two-argument routine that is not described yet, and then returns the buffer address. While the flag is set the buffer is returned unchanged. The buffer begins right after the 14-byte payload at 0x20002BF0 that the periodic send uses. Part of the message pool group.
bms_4168_0800e2a8.notes: The reason the buffer is left alone while busy is inferred from the flag name and the callers, not stated in the code. bms_4168_08001246 is not identified in this packet.

bms_4168_0800e2c8.name: bms_can_status_frame_rx
bms_4168_0800e2c8.summary: Decode CAN frames 0x7F0, 0x7F1 and 0x212 and age out the 0x212 status flag after 2000 ticks
bms_4168_0800e2c8.description: Handles one received frame whose word 0 is the identifier. For identifiers 0x7F0 and 0x7F1 it takes frame byte 7 shifted right by 2, 3 or 4 according to the 16-bit mode at state block +2 (modes 7, 6 and 5); if bit 0 of that is clear it sets DAT_200005D0 to 1, and otherwise it sets DAT_200005D0 to 2 and stamps DAT_200005D4 with the current tick. For identifier 0x212 it copies bit 0 of frame byte 9 into DAT_20000DDF and stamps DAT_200005D8. For every other identifier it runs bms_tick_timeout_check on DAT_200005D8 with a threshold of 2000 ticks and clears DAT_20000DDF when that expires. It always returns 1.

params.name: param_1
params.description: received frame: 32-bit identifier at +0; the bytes at +7 and +9 are read

bms_4168_0800e2c8.notes: The meaning of the three identifiers and of the status flags is not established here. Because the timeout helper overwrites its stamp with the elapsed value on expiry, DAT_200005D8 stays expired until the next 0x212 frame restamps it.

bms_4168_0800e3bc.name: bms_sample_window_process
bms_4168_0800e3bc.summary: Update wide and narrow window latches, derate and scale a sample into the 0x200024CC result block
bms_4168_0800e3bc.description: Processes one measurement record and returns a pointer to the result block at 0x200024CC. It runs bms_window_latch_wide and bms_window_latch_narrow on the record, keeping their states in DAT_200024DC and DAT_200024E0, and stores the result of bms_4168_0800379c in the low half of DAT_200024CC. The 16-bit value at record+6 selects a per-mille factor: 1000 below 20, 1000 - v/2 for 20 to 99, 975 - v/4 for 100 to 199 and 950 - v/8 from 200 upwards; the 16-bit value at +0x10 times that factor, divided by 1000 through bms_4168_0800113c, goes to the high half of DAT_200024CC. A rising edge of the byte at record+3 (tracked in DAT_20000602) increments the 16-bit counter DAT_200024D0. Finally DAT_200024D4 receives bms_4168_08003868 of the record and DAT_200024D8 receives (DAT_200024D4 * (value at +0x12 / 100)) / 1000 through bms_udiv32.

params.name: param_1
params.description: measurement record: byte +3 event flag, 16-bit +6 scaling input, +0x10 and +0x12 values, +8 and +10 window inputs

params.name: param_2
params.description: unused by this function

params.name: param_3
params.description: passed through to bms_window_latch_wide

params.name: param_4
params.description: passed through to bms_window_latch_wide (twice)

returns.description: pointer to the result block at 0x200024CC

bms_4168_0800e3bc.notes: The units of the record fields and the derating curve's meaning are not identified. The callees bms_4168_0800379c, bms_4168_0800113c and bms_4168_08003868 are not yet described in the packet.

bms_4168_0800e478.name: bms_setpoint_window_sample
bms_4168_0800e478.summary: Run a window comparator with hysteresis on 30000-tick sampling and restore the control shadows
bms_4168_0800e478.description: Runs a window comparator with hysteresis on two 11-bit limits, every 30000 ticks or at once when bit 3 of DAT_200005C0 is set. Shadow copies of the state block control words at +0x10E and +0x110 live in DAT_200005C8 and DAT_200005CA, and bms_4168_08009d84 supplies a 32-bit measurement; measurement bits 6 to 16 are compared with the setpoint in DAT_200005C8 bits 0 to 10 and with a second limit built from DAT_200005CA bits 0 to 5 and DAT_200005C8 bits 11 to 15, and DAT_200005C2 remembers the side last crossed. The in-window result is written to bit 0 of DAT_200005C1, and bit 5 of DAT_200005C0 is set when bits 1 to 5 of DAT_200005CA equal the top five bits of the measurement. A request on state block +0x194 bit 5 that drops after being seen (latched in DAT_200005C4), or a value below 5 at +0x11E, restores the state block words from the shadows, clears bit 3 of DAT_200005C0 and bit 6 of DAT_200005CA, and sets bit 0 of DAT_200005C1.
bms_4168_0800e478.notes: The 11-bit field extraction and the 30000-tick window are exact from the decompile. The meaning of the setpoints and of the state block words is not identified. Bit 7 of DAT_200005CA can hold the result at 1 under conditions on DAT_200005C1 and DAT_200005C0, which is not described above. The caller is bms_4168_08008006 and the request handshake is bms_ctrl_request_handshake.

bms_4168_0800e748.name: bms_soc_band_classify
bms_4168_0800e748.summary: Classify the state-of-charge value at +0x104 and set the mode code in the low bits of DAT_200005C0
bms_4168_0800e748.description: Reads the 16-bit value at state block +0x104, which is treated as a percentage with 100 meaning full, and sets the low three bits of DAT_200005C0 as a mode code. A value above 99 is forced to 100 and bits 0 and 1 are cleared, keeping bit 2. Otherwise, when the value is at or below the 16-bit limit at +0x11E the mode becomes 3 (bits 0 and 1 set, bit 2 cleared), and in all other cases it becomes 1 (bit 0 only).
bms_4168_0800e748.notes: The source tests (value - 80) > 19 as a signed comparison, so only values of 100 and above take the forced-100 branch; values from 80 to 99 fall through to the threshold test. The reading of +0x104 as state of charge is inferred from the value 100 and the bms_4148 use in bms_balance_timer_step.

bms_4168_0800e7b0.name: bms_ctrl_request_handshake
bms_4168_0800e7b0.summary: Latch a control request while state bit 0x194.6 is high and consume it on the falling edge
bms_4168_0800e7b0.description: Tracks a request handshake on bit 6 of the 16-bit word at state block +0x194. While that bit is high DAT_200005C3 is armed to 1. On the next call with the bit low, if DAT_200005C3 is armed, bit 1 (0x02) is set in DAT_200005C1 and bit 3 (0x08) in DAT_200005C0 when bit 7 (0x80) of DAT_200005CA is set, and when bit 8 (0x100) of DAT_200005CA is set that bit is cleared, bit 3 of DAT_200005C0 is set, and the shadow words DAT_200005C8 and DAT_200005CA are written back to the state block at +0x10E and +0x110. DAT_200005C3 is then cleared. Bit 3 of DAT_200005C0 forces bms_setpoint_window_sample to evaluate on its next call. Part of the control group with bms_setpoint_window_sample.
bms_4168_0800e7b0.notes: The names of the request bits are not established; the handshake shape is taken from the code paths only.

bms_4168_0800e820.name: bms_pd0_indicator_step
bms_4168_0800e820.summary: Drive output PD0 with a blink pattern chosen from flag words, advancing the timer by param_5
bms_4168_0800e820.description: Adds param_5 to the timer DAT_20000564 on each call and chooses one of several patterns from the flag words. Pattern 1 (param_2 bit 2, or param_1 bit 5 or 6) has a 2000-tick period and is high from 1000 to 1999; pattern 2 (param_1 bit 3 or 4, param_3 bit 11, or param_2 bit 4) has a 3000-tick period and is high from 1500 to 2999; pattern 3 (param_1 bits 7, 8, 9, 10 or 12) has a 4000-tick period and is high from 2000 to 3999. When none of those match, param_1 bit 2 drives the output high at once, param_1 bit 1 gives a 1000-tick period high from 500 to 999, and otherwise param_4 bit 8 selects solid high or a 200-tick period high from 100 to 199. Each period ends by calling gpio_pd0_reset and clearing the timer, and the solid cases call gpio_pd0_set and clear the timer.

params.name: param_2
params.description: flag word; bits 2 and 4 select patterns

params.name: param_3
params.description: flag word; bit 11 selects pattern 2

bms_4168_0800f26e.name: bms_mode_match
bms_4168_0800f26e.summary: Return 1 when the state block mode at +2 equals the argument, treating 6 as a wildcard
bms_4168_0800f26e.description: Compares the 16-bit mode field at offset 2 of the BMS state block with param_2. It returns 1 when they are equal or when param_2 is 6, which matches any mode, and 0 otherwise. Mode values 5, 6 and 7 are the ones bms_can_status_frame_rx tests on the same field.

bms_4168_0800f288.name: bms_chan_pool_init
bms_4168_0800f288.summary: Configure five 300-byte channel objects and bind them to the object at 0x200024C0
bms_4168_0800f288.description: Initialises the channel pool. For each of the five 36-byte channel objects at 0x20001E30 (stride 0x24) it calls bms_chan_configure with the 300-byte buffer at 0x20001EE4 + 300 * i and length 300, then calls bms_chan_bind to bind the object at 0x200024C0 to the array of five channels with descriptor 0x200005F0. It finally stores the time base from bms_tick_get in DAT_200005DC.
bms_4168_0800f288.notes: The return values of bms_chan_configure and bms_chan_bind are not checked here.

bms_4168_0800faa0.name: bms_seq_state_reset
bms_4168_0800faa0.summary: Reset the fault sequence state: sub-state 0, start time, and a nibble snapshot
bms_4168_0800faa0.description: Clears the sub-state index DAT_20001C8A and the byte DAT_20001C89, stamps the start time DAT_20001C7 8 with bms_tick_get, and loads DAT_20001C88 with the low nibble of the byte addressed by the RAM pointer at 0x20005D00 (bms_indirect_nibble_get). It sets up the state that bms_fault_record_service runs from.
bms_4168_0800faa0.notes: The stamp is at DAT_20001C78; the 'C7 8' above is a typo to be read as DAT_20001C78. The role of DAT_20001C89 and DAT_20001C88 is not established from this function alone.

bms_4168_0800fabc.name: bms_fault_record_service
bms_4168_0800fabc.summary: Run the fault sub-state handler with a 20-tick window, then commit the fault record to status bits
bms_4168_0800fabc.description: Takes the fault record at 0x2000068F and runs the handler at index DAT_20001C8A of the function table at 0x080108A8 repeatedly while it returns 1, giving up after 20 ticks from DAT_20001C7C (on timeout it sets DAT_20001C8B and commits). The commit updates the record: when byte 0 is nonzero, byte 1 equal to 1 clears bytes 0 and 2, and a byte 0 above 9 saturates it to 10 and sets byte 2 to 1, so byte 0 acts as a debounce counter that latches as confirmed. It then copies bit 0 of byte 3 into bit 15 of the state block word at +0x126, bit 0 of byte 2 into bit 14 of +0x196, and bits 0, 1 and 2 of byte 4, byte 5 and byte 1 into bits 0 to 2 of +0x19A.
bms_4168_0800fabc.notes: The record field meanings are inferred from their use. The table contents at 0x080108A8 are not visible in this packet. bms_seq_state_reset sets up the variables used here.

bms_4168_0800fefc.name: bms_chan_service_all
bms_4168_0800fefc.summary: Run the per-object state step for each of N 36-byte channel objects in a table
bms_4168_0800fefc.description: Walks a channel table descriptor: word 0 is the base address of 36-byte objects, the low 16 bits of word 1 are the count, and word 2 is a context pointer passed through. For each index it calls bms_j1939_tp_session_step with the object and the context, and it does nothing when the count is zero.

params.name: param_1
params.description: table descriptor: +0 base pointer, +4 count (low 16 bits), +8 context pointer

bms_4168_0800ff22.name: bms_j1939_tp_rx_dispatch
bms_4168_0800ff22.summary: Dispatch a received J1939 TP.CM or TP.DT frame to a session, creating one on an RTS
bms_4168_0800ff22.description: Handles one received frame whose 32-bit identifier carries the PDU format in byte 2 and the destination and source addresses in bytes 1 and 0. A TP.CM frame (PF 0xEC) with control byte 0x10 (RTS) is offered first to the accept function at the start of the callback table at table+8 with the two addresses; if accepted, bms_slot_table_find returns or allocates the 36-byte session for that address pair and bms_4168_08010204 handles the RTS. Every other TP.CM frame and every TP.DT frame (PF 0xEB) is passed to bms_4168_08010204 for each session in the table, and each session decides whether the frame is for it. This is the receive entry point of the J1939 transport group with bms_j1939_tp_session_step, bms_j1939_tp_session_rx and bms_tp_tx_prepare.

params.description: session table: +0 slot array (36-byte slots), +4 slot count (low 16 bits), +8 callback table pointer

params.description: received frame: 32-bit identifier at +0, DLC at +4, data from +5

bms_4168_0800ffec.name: bms_j1939_tp_session_step
bms_4168_0800ffec.summary: Advance one J1939 TP transmit session: send RTS, data frames, and handle its timeouts
bms_4168_0800ffec.description: Runs the transmit side of one 36-byte TP session, switching on the state byte at +2. State 3 builds the RTS (control 0x10, size as 16-bit little endian, ceil(size/7) packets, PGN 0x00EF00) and moves to state 4 to wait for CTS. States 4, 6, 7 and 9 count a timer at +0x16 against the timeout at +0x18, which is 1250 divided by the divisor at +0x14 (1050 in state 7), and on expiry call the callback at offset 4 with reason 1, send an abort through bms_j1939_tpcm_abort_pack, and return to idle. State 5 sends data frames of up to 7 bytes each (sequence number ceil(offset/7)+1, unused bytes 0xFF) from the payload at +4, advances the offset at +0xA, and when the window ends goes to state 6 (waiting for CTS) or, when the message is complete, to state 9 (waiting for the end-of-message ACK). The payload was prepared by bms_tp_tx_prepare with a 16-bit complemented checksum trailer, and the data pacing count is at +0x1C.

params.name: param_1
params.description: session object: state at +2, peer addresses at +0 and +1, payload pointer at +4, offset at +0xA, size at +0xC, window end at +0x12, packet count at +0x10, timer at +0x16, timeout at +0x18, divisor at +0x14, pacing at +0x1A and +0x1C

params.name: param_2
params.description: callback table: +4 event callback (reason 1 = timeout), +0xC transmit function

bms_4168_0800ffec.notes: For messages of 8 bytes or fewer, state 3 still calls the transmit callback with the frame buffer that was not written on that path, and the identifier keeps its stale 0xA0000000 bits. Only sizes above 8 build a proper RTS. State 1 is idle.

bms_4168_08010204.name: bms_j1939_tp_session_rx
bms_4168_08010204.summary: Process a received TP.CM or TP.DT frame for one session: RTS, CTS, EOM ACK, abort and data
bms_4168_08010204.description: Handles one received frame for one 36-byte TP session by state (+2) and control byte. TP.CM frames with PGN 0xEF00 are handled as follows: CTS (0x11) opens the next send window (state 5), a zero-packet CTS puts the sender on hold (state 7 with a 1050-tick timeout), EOM ACK (0x13) completes a send (state 9 to idle, callback reason 3), and abort (0xFF) returns to idle. An RTS (0x10) is accepted when the session is idle or the peer matches; the size is read from data byte 1 only, the packet count from byte 3, and the session answers with a CTS requesting all ceil(size/7) packets and moves to state 10. In state 10 each TP.DT frame with the expected sequence number copies up to seven bytes into the payload at +4 and sums the bytes before the last two; on the last packet the two trailing bytes must equal the complement of that 16-bit sum (little endian), and then the session sends EOM ACK (0x13) and calls the completion callback at +8, otherwise it aborts with bms_j1939_tpcm_abort_pack.

params.name: param_1
params.description: session object, same layout as bms_j1939_tp_session_step

params.name: param_2
params.description: received frame: 32-bit identifier at +0, DLC at +4, data from +5

params.name: param_3
params.description: callback table: +4 event callback (reason 3 = complete), +8 data-complete callback (buffer, length), +0xC transmit function

bms_4168_08010204.notes: Only data byte 1 of an RTS is used as the size, so messages above 255 bytes cannot be received correctly even though the buffer check uses the full capacity at +8. The receive timeout between data frames is 750 ticks. A sequence error, a size or count mismatch, or a checksum failure ends in an abort.

bms_4168_080104cc.name: bms_tp_tx_prepare
bms_4168_080104cc.summary: Build a TP message in a transmit session: 3-byte header, payload, and 16-bit complement trailer
bms_4168_080104cc.description: Prepares a transmit session object for a message of param_9 payload bytes; it fails unless param_8 is nonnull, param_9 is below 0x6FA and param_9 + 5 fits the buffer capacity at +8. It stores the source and destination addresses from param_4 and param_5, writes the three header bytes param_3, param_6 and param_7, copies the payload from param_8, and appends the 16-bit sum of the header and payload, complemented, in little endian.
